claims.text: A tailored refractory high-entropy alloy interlayer with an intermediate coefficient of thermal expansion can effectively bridge tungsten and CuCrZr.
Directly bonded tungsten and CuCrZr suffer from severe thermal-expansion mismatch.
Directly bonded tungsten and CuCrZr suffer from chemical incompatibility.
Adjusting the proportions of Ta, Cr, V, or Hf in a refractory HEA can produce an intermediate coefficient of thermal expansion.
Adjusting the proportions of Ta, Cr, V, or Hf can provide favorable bonding characteristics for a W/CuCrZr interlayer.
Fusion-reactor service exposes the joint to high heat flux, rapid thermal cycling, and intense radiation.
The HEA interlayer can act as a gradient mediator that eases the thermal-expansion mismatch between W and CuCrZr.
The HEA interlayer can improve bonding at both the W/interlayer and interlayer/CuCrZr interfaces.
Reducing thermal-expansion mismatch through composition tuning lowers residual-stress buildup in the joint.
Composition tuning of the HEA interlayer mitigates chemical incompatibility between W and CuCrZr.
Lower residual stress and improved chemical compatibility enhance the mechanical integrity of the W/CuCrZr joint.
The compositionally tuned HEA interlayer improves resistance to radiation damage.
Compared with direct bonding, the HEA interlayer will produce a more stable W/CuCrZr interface with fewer interfacial cracks.
Compared with direct bonding, the HEA interlayer will enhance joint durability under thermal and radiation stresses.
Existing directly bonded W/CuCrZr interfaces exhibit high residual stresses, interfacial cracking, and joint failure under extreme conditions.
Successful implementation depends on identifying an appropriate HEA composition and reproducible production-scale processing conditions.
Composition or processing deviations may fail to mediate thermal mismatch or may create new compatibility problems during prolonged irradiation.
The exact HEA composition required to balance thermal expansion and chemical compatibility is uncertain.
Long-term performance of the proposed interlayer under irradiation and thermal cycling is uncertain.
